rv.q: She has already scaled a new peak.
It's a mind-bending, inexorable helter skelter into hell, surreal as a nightmare
Jones's production is a sort of infernal anxiety machine, percussive and remorseless
This is a small qualm in an exceptional production that proves Machinal has lost none of its potency.
The outstanding acting makes up for much of that.
It’s theatrical torture that does to the viewer what the State of New York did to our poor, deluded heroine.
You rarely see such meticulous, detailed work in the theatre.
Rosie Sheehy’s performance is an astonishing feat.
A song about freedom sung by a prisoner (Daniel Bowerbank), condemned just like the Young Woman, is both cathartic and delightful.
Whether it’s worth the emotional investment required on both sides of the fourth wall for its equivocating payoff is moot.
Everything is icky, our spectatorship as audience members watching a woman in distress feels intrusive and uncomfortable.
Jones' visceral production is imaginatively staged and the impressive ensemble cast pull out all the stops.
It’s an achievement, of sorts, but not one for all tastes.

cn.t: Jones's visceral production of Treadwell's 1928 expressionist play earns acclaim for its meticulous staging and Sheehy's fearless performance, though critics split on whether the relentlessly bleak, mechanical style proves brilliant or punishing.

vr.q: The 1 hour 50 minutes without interval fly by in this gripping production. I give Machinal four stars.
